questions.prompt: 1  Alfred Wegener proposed the theory of continental drift. Which of the following observations did he use to support his theory?
options: Fossils could be found in different countries.
Africa and South America seemed to fit together like jigsaw pieces.
Rocks had magnetic striping near the ocean ridges.
The sea floor seemed to be made at the ridges.
questions.explanation: The apparent fit of Africa and South America is the best stated Wegener observation. Mere fossil presence in different countries is insufficient without specific matching distributions.

questions.prompt: 2 Harry Hess proposed a mechanism by which Wegener’s continental drift could occur. Hess’s theory was called:
options: plate tectonics
continental drift
seafloor spreading
subduction
ocean trenches forming by collision of plates
the crust subducting
plates moving by sliding past each other
the crust cracking and subsiding
questions.explanation: Rifting stretches,fractures and can cause subsidence of the crust/lithosphere.

questions.prompt: 5 Evidence of spreading of the crust at ocean ridges resulted from:
options: seismic activity in the Earth’s crust
differences in density of oceanic and continental crust
subduction of plates at collision boundaries
reversals in the Earth’s magnetic field
questions.explanation: Alternating magnetic polarity recorded symmetrically across ocean ridges supports seafloor spreading;reversals alone need the spatial rock pattern.

questions.prompt: 6 Tectonic plates nowadays can be measured accurately using:
options: a tectonic scale
GPS and satellites
a seismometer
microwave and mobile phone technology
questions.explanation: Satellite geodesy/GPS tracks changing positions and thus plate motion.
